correctness.rationale: For c in [-1/2,1/2], use omega(z)=z v(z) to express preSchwarzian(z)=v+c z v² and S_f=(1+2czv)v' +(c-1/2)v²-czv³-(1/2)c²z²v^4. Apply Schwarz–Pick |v'|<=(1-|v|²)/(1-|z|²). With r=|z|,s=|v|,u=1-r², for c>=0 the upper envelope F_+(c,r,s) is convex quadratic in c, with explicit nonnegative 1-F_+(0,r,s) and 1-F_+(1/2,r,s) polynomial decompositions. For c=-d the exact 1-F_- identity is (r-dus)²+us²(1/2-d-d²)+ur²s²(d²+d+1/2)+drus³(1+r²-(drus)/2); all terms nonnegative iff d<=d_*=(sqrt3-1)/2 in the demonstrated interval. Equality/uniform gap forces z->0,v(0)=0 and |v'(0)|=1; Schwarz equality then v=e^{i theta}z, yielding exactly normalized rotation family and norm 1. For d>d_* choose disk automorphism with v(r)=-s and r=ds; alignment makes F_- exact and its s² coefficient d²+d-1/2 positive, establishing a counterexample for sufficiently small s. Ahlfors–Weill then supplies K<=3 as sufficient, not optimal. Independent SymPy verified the full F_- SOS identity and critical expansion exactly.
risks: Finite algebraic identity checks do not themselves prove the uniform hyperbolic bound; the sign, boundary compactness and Schwarz rigidity arguments provide analytic proof.
Negative c targets need not be positive-real-part Ma–Minda convex targets; claim is subordination only.
K<=3 is sufficient; failure of S bound below cutoff says nothing about optimal quasiconformal dilatation.
